top_level_objectives: Identify the major three-dimensional components of DNA, including the sugar-phosphate backbones, nitrogenous bases, and helical arrangement.
Explain antiparallel strand orientation and 5' to 3' versus 3' to 5' directionality in DNA.
Describe complementary base-pairing rules and hydrogen bonding between A-T and G-C.
Trace the major steps of DNA replication, including unwinding, strand stabilization, leading and lagging strand synthesis, and ligation.
Explain why DNA replication is semiconservative and how DNA structure dictates replication asymmetry.

scenes.scene_name: Overview of the DNA Double Helix
scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the overall 3D architecture of DNA as a double helix with two strands wrapped around a common axis.
key_visuals: A large rotatable DNA double helix
Bases projecting inward between the strands
student_actions: Identify the outer backbones and inner bases

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students distinguish the molecular components of each strand and recognize complementary pairing rules.
key_visuals: Individual nucleotides highlighted in the helix
Hydrogen bonds shown between paired bases
student_actions: Select bases to reveal their names
Compare the number of hydrogen bonds in A-T versus G-C pairs

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how strand directionality creates antiparallel orientation in the double helix.
key_visuals: Aligned paired strands with opposite orientations
student_actions: Trace each strand from one end to the other
Label one strand 5' to 3' and the other 3' to 5'
Explain how opposite orientation supports base pairing

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the beginning of DNA replication by showing helix unwinding and stabilization of separated strands.
key_visuals: Single-strand binding proteins attached to exposed strands
student_actions: Trigger helicase movement to unzip the helix
Observe where the replication fork forms
Identify the role of single-strand binding proteins

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how DNA polymerase synthesizes new DNA differently on the two templates because synthesis proceeds only 5' to 3'.
key_visuals: DNA polymerase enzymes on both template strands
Discontinuous Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand
student_actions: Follow polymerase as it adds nucleotides to each new strand
Relate strand direction to why the two daughter strands are made differently

scenes.brief_purpose: Conclude replication by showing ligation of Okazaki fragments and the final semiconservative products.
key_visuals: DNA ligase sealing gaps between Okazaki fragments
Original parental strands visually distinguished from newly synthesized strands
student_actions: Seal lagging-strand fragments into a continuous strand
Sort parental versus new strands in each daughter helix
State why the final result is called semiconservative replication
